'''Barbara Jacak''' ({{IPA|pol|ˈjat͡sak}}) is a nuclear [[physicist]] who uses heavy ion collisions for fundamental studies of hot, dense nuclear matter. She is director of the Nuclear Science Division, [[Lawrence Berkeley National Laboratory]], and a professor of physics at [[University of California, Berkeley|UC Berkeley]].<ref name="ARCS">{{cite web|url=https://www.arcsfoundation.org/scholars/alumni-hall-fame|title=ARCS Foundation>>ARCS Alumni Hall of Fame|publisher=ARCS|accessdate=January 16, 2019}}</ref> Before going to Berkeley, she was a member of the Department of Physics and Astronomy at [[Stony Brook University]], where she held the rank of distinguished professor. She is a leading member of the collaboration that built and operates the [[PHENIX]] detector, one of the large detectors that operated at the [[Relativistic Heavy Ion Collider]] at [[Brookhaven National Laboratory]], and was involved in the discovery of the quark gluon plasma and its strongly coupled, liquid-like behavior. Throughout her career she has served on many advisory committees and boards, including the [[United States National Research Council|National Research Council]] Committee on Nuclear Physics, and the ''[[Physical Review]] C'' editorial board.<ref name="APS bio"/>

==Physics career==
Jacak started her career at [[Michigan State University]], where she completed her Ph.D. in chemical physics in 1984 working at the [[National Superconducting Cyclotron Laboratory]] (NSCL).<ref name="ACAP bio"/> She began working at [[Los Alamos National Laboratory]] in 1984 as a [https://web.archive.org/web/20130117063843/http://t8web.lanl.gov/postdocs.html J.R. Oppenheimer Fellow]. She became a laboratory staff member in 1987, continuing until 1996. During her time at Los Alamos, she also taught as an adjunct associate professor at the [[University of New Mexico]], from 1994 to 1996.<ref name="APS bio"/> In 1997 she joined [[Stony Brook University]] to lead the [http://www.stonybrook.edu/nsl/phenix.html Relativistic Heavy Ion Group], affiliated with the PHENIX experiment.<ref name="APS bio"/> In 2008, she was appointed to the rank of distinguished professor.<ref name="ACAP bio">{{cite news|url=https://history.aip.org/phn/11602009.html|title=ACAP bio}}</ref><ref name="SBU press release"/>

Since January, 2015, Jacak has been the director of the Nuclear Science Division at Lawrence Berkeley Laboratories. She also holds joint appointments as faculty senior scientist at Berkeley Lab and as professor of physics at UC Berkeley.<ref name=ucb>{{cite web|url=https://physics.berkeley.edu/people/faculty/barbara-jacak|title=Barbara Jacak: Professor of Physics|publisher=UC Berkeley Physics Department|accessdate=January 16, 2019}}</ref>

===PHENIX Collaboration===
Jacak has been a member of the [[PHENIX detector|PHENIX]] Collaboration since the detector was first proposed.<ref>{{cite news|url=http://archive.sciencewatch.com/ana/st/hadron/11marSThad_BNL/|title=Science Watch Interview|accessdate=January 16, 2019}}</ref> She served on the Detector Council from 1992 to 1994 and the Executive Council from 1994 to 2006.<ref name="APS bio"/> In December 2006 she was elected as spokesperson of PHENIX.<ref name="SBU press release"/> She served as spokesperson for two consecutive terms, stepping down at the end of 2012. Under her leadership as spokesperson, PHENIX published over 60 papers in peer-reviewed journals and graduated over 90 Ph.D.'s from institutions around the world.<ref>{{cite news|url=http://inspirehep.net/search?ln=en&ln=en&p=find+exp+bnl-rhic-phenix+and+%28j+phrva+or+j+prlta+or+j+phlta%29+and+%28d+2007+or+d+2008+or+d+2009+or+d+2010+or+d+2011+or+d+2012%29&of=hb&action_search=Search&sf=&so=d&rm=&rg=25&sc=0|title=INSPIRE-HEP list|accessdate=January 16, 2019}}</ref><ref>{{cite news|url=http://www.phenix.bnl.gov/WWW/publish/jacak/sp/theses/Theses.pdf|title=PHENIX Theses table}}</ref> She oversaw the successful installation of three major detector upgrades, as well as several smaller upgrades.<ref>{{cite news|url=https://www.phenix.bnl.gov/plans.html|title=PHENIX Beam Use Proposals|accessdate=January 16, 2019}}</ref>

===ALICE Collaboration===
Prof. Jacak has been a member of the [[ALICE experiment|ALICE]] Collaboration since March 2015. She is the team leader of the UC Berkeley group.<ref>{{cite news|author=Adriana Telesca|author2=Panagiotis Charitos|url=http://alicematters.web.cern.ch/?q=New_CB_2015|title=News from the ALICE Collaboration Board|date=April 24, 2015|accessdate=January 16, 2019}}</ref>

*2009 &ndash; Elected to be a member of the [[National Academy of Sciences]]<ref>{{cite news|url=http://commcgi.cc.stonybrook.edu/am2/publish/General_University_News_2/SBU_Distinguished_Professor_And_Internationally_Renowned_Nuclear_Physicist_Elected_To_The_National_Academy_Of_Sciences.shtml|title=SBU press release|year=2009}}</ref>
*2019 &ndash; ''[[Tom W. Bonner Prize in Nuclear Physics]]''<ref>{{cite web|url=https://today.lbl.gov/2018/09/13/barbara-jacak-wins-aps-2019-bonner-prize/|title=APS to Announce Barbara Jacak as Winner of Bonner Prize|publisher=Berkeley Lab|date=September 13, 2018|accessdate=January 16, 2019}}</ref>
